mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 1.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected future equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate months, or the FEDFUNDS spike is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.2 percentage points is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market tightness reduces recession risk and boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: In 50+ test windows, no significant positive return occurs after UNRATE rises ≥ 0.2pp (Granger causality rejected, or p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (units of housing starts) of at least 5% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the bounce signals renewed builder confidence and economic recovery.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops ≥ 5% in month t, then HOUST in month t+1 > HOUST[t]
regime_hint: Rebound from deep contraction in housing activity
failure_condition: Across 30 historical rebound events, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO above 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side expansion, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as excess capacity suppresses earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month increase ≥ 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 40+ such supply-side acceleration events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (mean ≥ 0, p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as lower policy rates encourage risk-on sentiment and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Across 20 such accommodation episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market employment) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% each, accompanied by UNRATE below 7%, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual labor and demand strength.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS ↑ ≥ 2%, RSAFS ↑ ≥ 2%, UNRATE < 7% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening and robust retail demand
failure_condition: In 50+ interaction windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in CPIAUCSL below 200 (index level) followed by a sustained increase to 210 over the next two months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates higher inflation and tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 200, then CPIAUCSL rises to ≥ 210 over next two months
regime_hint: Inflation acceleration detected in the CPI index
failure_condition: Across 30 such inflation acceleration episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean ≥ 0, p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP momentum) shows a double-digit monthly increase for two consecutive months in a post-recession context, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 20-day forward return as the market anticipates overheating and potential policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month increase ≥ 12% for two consecutive months and recession is no longer detected
regime_hint: Economic momentum in a non-recession environment
failure_condition: In 40 such momentum episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (mean ≥ 0, p-value > 0.05).
